title: Local Refinement from Round-1 Baseline with ±10 nm Perturbation Cap
scientific_hypothesis: The round-1 gradient_thickness candidate (0.9405 score) represents a near-optimal interference structure; restricting optimization to ±10 nm perturbations per layer will preserve the alternating high/low spatial sequence while fine-tuning thicknesses to recover or exceed the round-1 performance without the interference breakdown observed in rounds 2-3.
design_principle: Local optimization around a verified high-performing baseline prevents the optimizer from exploring thickness combinations that cause adjacent layers to converge or swap optical order, which the feedback identifies as the direct cause of interference breakdown.
proposed_topology: exactly 36 finite layers from the incident side: Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2
manufacturing_considerations: ±10 nm perturbation bound preserves manufacturable thickness distribution
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
Local optimization preserves verified interference structure
expected_advantages: Preserves round-1 interference structure that achieved 0.9405 score
Prevents adjacent layer thickness convergence that caused rounds 2-3 degradation
known_risks: May be trapped in local optimum if round-1 baseline was not globally optimal
±10 nm bound may be too restrictive if larger adjustments are needed
